    Verified component example

    Keep token features on a comparable scale

    1. 1
      Input

      Two example feature vectors: [3, 4] and [30, 40]. The second is ten times larger.

    2. 2
      Normalize

      The repository’s RMSNorm layer divides each vector by its root mean square, with the initial learned scale set to 1.

    3. 3
      Verified output

      Both become approximately [0.8485, 1.1314], preserving their proportions at a comparable scale.

    Executed with the linked repository’s PyTorch layer. This demonstrates a model component; it does not require trained weights.

    Run this example +

    Requires Python 3.10+ and PyTorch 2.x. Download rmsnorm_demo.py into your working folder, then run:

    git clone https://github.com/weichaohuang1220/llm-from-scratch.git
cd llm-from-scratch
git checkout f7f344204c90483357f4aed7687f0c8063323eeb
cd ..
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install torch
python rmsnorm_demo.py ./llm-from-scratch

    Recorded output, rounded to four decimal places:

    [3.0, 4.0] -> [0.8485, 1.1314]
[30.0, 40.0] -> [0.8485, 1.1314]
PASS: the two scaled inputs normalize to approximately the same vector.

    ChatMind · AI Agent System

    2025.12 – 2026.02

    Built a multi-step AI agent with tool calling and knowledge-base retrieval using pgvector, model switching, and streamed task progress via SSE.

    Java · Spring AI · PostgreSQL

    Document Q&A walkthrough

    Can I book Cedar for 90 minutes?

    1. 1
      Provide the guide

      Upload room-guide.md and attach its knowledge base to the agent. The sample policy limits bookings to 60 minutes.

    2. 2
      Ask and retrieve

      “Can I book Cedar for 90 minutes?” KnowledgeTool retrieves relevant sections and reranks the candidates.

    3. 3
      Expected answer

      “No. The limit is 60 minutes. Choose a shorter available slot in the room calendar.”

    Fictional policy, grounded in the provided file. Source-checked walkthrough; the full backend and model flow has not been run here.

    Try with your ChatMind setup +

    Requires a configured ChatMind backend and UI, an initialized PostgreSQL/pgvector database, Ollama with bge-m3, and working DeepSeek access for answering and reranking.

    1. Download room-guide.md. Create a knowledge base named Room Guide, upload the file, and confirm it is indexed.
    2. Create an agent using deepseek-chat and attach Room Guide in its knowledge-base settings. KnowledgeTool is built in.
    3. Use the instruction below, then ask: “Can I book Cedar for 90 minutes? What should I do instead?”
    Answer in English. Use KnowledgeTool to consult the attached Room Guide
before answering. Base your answer on retrieved text and name the source
section. If the guide does not contain the answer, say so.
Do not make a reservation.

    Check that the answer rejects 90 minutes, gives the 60-minute limit, and names the Cedar meeting room booking policy. Wording may vary.

    Full setup notes and checks · View the retrieval tool ↗

    Explore the full architecture +

    Follow one question through the whole system. Select a step to inspect its path.

    Scroll sideways to explore the full diagram.

    1 / 7 · Prepare the knowledge base

    Upload room-guide.md. Split it at headings, embed section titles with bge-m3, and store the chunks and vectors before asking a question.

    2 / 7 · Send the room-policy question

    “Can I book Cedar for 90 minutes?” The React UI submits the message; the backend saves it and builds the agent runtime from its settings.

    3 / 7 · Choose the next action

    The selected model helps the Agent plan and decide which tool to call. Conversation history is available as context; memory features apply when needed.

    4 / 7 · Call KnowledgeTool

    The Agent requests the attached guide. bge-m3 embeds the query; pgvector retrieves up to five nearest candidate sections.

    5 / 7 · Return the relevant policy

    DeepSeek reranks the candidates and keeps up to three. The returned text includes Cedar’s 60-minute limit. Reranking failure falls back to the original order.

    6 / 7 · Generate a grounded answer

    The Agent passes the retrieved context back to its model. Expected answer: “No. Cedar bookings are limited to 60 minutes; choose a shorter available slot.”

    7 / 7 · Show progress and the answer

    SSE carries planning, execution and generated-message events back to the UI throughout the request. This final highlight follows the return path; streaming does not wait until the end.
